8.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you classify a periprosthetic femoral fracture?"
- "**Vancouver** → site: A trochanters · B stem · C below → **stem stability** → bone stock."
- "**B1** stable → fix · **B2** loose, good bone → revise · **B3** loose, poor bone → rebuild."
- "Intraoperative → modified Vancouver A–C, subtypes **1 perforation · 2 crack · 3 displaced**."

### Definition & risk factors
- **Periprosthetic fracture** = fracture next to an implant, intra- or postoperative · acetabulum or femur
- Rising → more arthroplasties in younger, more active patients
[[FIG: Fig 8.1 · 8.1
- Aims of treatment → **fracture union** + **implant stability**

| Patient | Implant & technique |
|---|---|
| Age · **osteoporosis** · RA (rheumatoid arthritis) · **Paget** · DDH (developmental dysplasia of the hip) | **Osteolysis**, loosening · **cementless** stem → more fractures, esp. elderly women (Campbell) |
| Abnormal femoral shape → difficult insertion | Extensive instrumentation · **revision** → bone loss, stress risers, cement removal |

- Implant bigger than the last broach → wedge splits the femur → stop, check

#### Assess the patient
- Pain before the fall → pre-existing **loosening** or osteolysis → chapter 07
- Pain + stiffness since surgery → **infection** work-up → chapter 06
- Neurovascular exam · implant records → type, company, size
- Neurological disorder → large head, tripolar or **dual mobility** → chapter 05

### Intraoperative fractures
- Incidence → **1.7%** of primaries · **12%** of revisions (Campbell)
- Cementless press-fit stem (oversized) > cemented stem (smaller than the broach) · revisions highest

| Step | Trigger → twisting or wedging force |
|---|---|
| **Neck cut** | too high → keep one fingerbreadth above lesser trochanter · head out before the cut in a stiff hip |
| **Reaming, broaching** | rigid reamer or rasp · press-fit stem bigger than the canal: rasped 6, size 7 forced |
| **Stem length** | long straight stem against the **anterior bow** |
| **Reduction** | trial or final reduction twisting the femur |
| **Revision** | poor bone stock · cement removal · impaction grafting |

#### Prevention — the lecture's main point
- Adequate **exposure** · no force in osteoporotic bone · **templating** · trial first (Prof Kassem)
[[FIG: Fig 8.2 · 8.1
- Stiff hip → cut the neck before dislocating · look for a crack after each broach
- Stuck revision stem → **ETO** (extended trochanteric osteotomy) → controlled beats uncontrolled fracture
[[FIG: Fig 8.3 · 8.1
- Fragile femur → **distal cerclage** before reaming → prevents shattering
[[FIG: Fig 8.4 · 8.1

CLINICAL PEARL — found a crack?
- **Calcar split** → stem out, cable, reinsert · still unstable → bypass to the diaphysis (Miller)
- Suspected fracture → film in theatre or at once → undisplaced distal cracks are missed

### Postoperative fractures
- Incidence → **1%** primaries · **4%** revisions · usually a low-energy fall (Prof Kassem)
- Mean time to fracture → **7.3 years** Swedish register · **8.1 years** Mayo Clinic
- Stem tip = **stress riser** → stiff stem, flexible bone → late fractures there (Miller)
- Risks → **osteolysis**, loosening · **varus** stem → more lateral cortex bending

#### Prevention is the best treatment
- No cortical defects or malalignment · serial films → catch osteolysis before it breaks
- Treat **osteoporosis** and fall risk → most late fractures follow a simple fall

### Modified Vancouver — intraoperative

| Type | Site | Treatment by subtype (Prof Kassem) |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | proximal metaphysis | A1 → graft: head, reamings · A2 → metaphyseal cerclage · A3 → cables or plate |
| **B** | diaphysis around the stem | B1 → longer stem + graft · B2 stable → cerclage · B2 unstable, B3 → longer stem + fixation ± graft |
| **C** | distal to the stem | C1 → cortical strut · C2 → cerclage or plate · C3 → **ORIF** (open reduction, internal fixation) |

- Subtypes fit **every** type → **1** perforation · **2** undisplaced crack · **3** displaced, unstable
[[FIG: Fig 8.5 · 8.1
- Location = what is threatened · subtype = will a simple cable hold
[[FIG: Fig 8.6 · 8.1
- Perforation → stem passes it by **≥2 cortical diameters** → load goes to intact bone
[[FIG: Fig 8.7 · 8.1
- Type C → strut, cerclage or plate · the stem is left alone
[[FIG: Fig 8.8 · 8.1

#### Case
- Intraoperative type B → cerclage wires + cementless modular **Wagner** stem (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 8.9 · 8.1

### Vancouver — postoperative
- Most important postoperative system → **location → stem fixation → bone stock** (Prof Abdel Karim)

| Type | Site | Stem & bone (Campbell) |
|---|---|---|
| **A-G · A-L** | greater · lesser trochanter | — |
| **B1** | around or just below the stem | stable |
| **B2** | around or just below the stem | loose · good bone |
| **B3** | around or just below the stem | loose · poor bone: osteolysis, comminution |
| **C** | well below the stem | not involved |

- Type B → commonest and hardest · **B1** fix · **B2** revise · **B3** reconstruct
[[FIG: Fig 8.10 · 8.1
- **UCS** (Unified Classification System) → Vancouver logic for every joint · differs → know both

PITFALL — is there a Vancouver D?
- Course → A, B, C only · Campbell → **D = interprosthetic**, between hip and knee implants
- Say → "Vancouver is A–C; between two implants = **D**, same stability rules"

#### Work-up — B1 or B2?
- Pre-fracture pain · films of the **whole femur** · **CT** · stability test in theatre
[[FIG: Fig 8.11 · 8.1
- Films → long AP + long lateral + **AP pelvis** for offset · pelvis alone misses the tip
[[FIG: Fig 8.12 · 8.1
- **CT** → stock, extension, seating, wear, comminution · bone scan → false positive after fracture
[[FIG: Fig 8.13 · 8.1

EXAM PEARL — B1 on film, B2 at surgery
- The fracture breaks the fixation interface → films miss it → test the stem in theatre
- Many "B1" prove **B2** → revise · broken **cement mantle**, lucent lines, lytic bone = loose (Miller; Prof Sherif Khaled)

### Level-based systems
- Handbook ("American Academy") → types **1–5** by level · no stem stability → cannot choose treatment

| Type | Level |
|---|---|
| **1 · 2** | above · opposite lesser trochanter → proximal third of the stem |
| **3** | opposite middle third · non-comminuted |
| **4** | opposite lower third · comminuted |
| **5** | distal to the tip |

- **Johansson**, **Bethea** → older level systems, same flaw → in the viva lead with **Vancouver**

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Where → loose? → bone · B1 fix, B2 revise, B3 rebuild · perforation → bypass 2 cortices**

8.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you treat a Vancouver B fracture?"
- "**Loose stem + fracture = revision** → a plate cannot hold around a moving stem."
- "B1 → **locking plate** + cables overlapping the stem · B2 → **long diaphyseal stem**."
- "B3 → long stem + graft, or **proximal femoral replacement** · C → plate, stem stays."

### Before any revision
- Rule out **infection** → cultures always · **spacer** on standby → chapter 06
- **Multidisciplinary team** → neurology, cardiology, anaesthesia, ICU (intensive care unit)
- Uncontrolled **diabetes** (glucose ≈400) → postpone · **anticoagulants** matter

### Vancouver A
- Undisplaced → **conservative** · **A-L** → conservative unless the **calcar** goes, loosening the stem
- Displaced, ≥**2 cm** → **cerclage wires**, plate or **claw plate** (Prof Kassem)
[[FIG: Fig 8.14 · 8.2
- **A-G** → fixed to keep **abductor** function · nonunion → limp, instability
[[FIG: Fig 8.15 · 8.2
- **Atraumatic** GT (greater trochanter) fracture → **osteolysis** → graft · massive → no ORIF (Miller)

### Vancouver B

| Type | Treatment (Prof Kassem) |
|---|---|
| **B1** | stem kept → **ORIF**: locking plate + proximal cables |
| **B2** | stem out → **long stem** → fracture fixation |
| **B3** | long stem + reconstruction · impossible → **proximal femoral replacement** |

- Examples → B1 plate · B2 porous-coated stem + cables · B3 tapered fluted stem
[[FIG: Fig 8.16 · 8.2

#### B1 — fix around the stable stem
- Long locking plate → unicortical screws + cables proximally · bicortical distally
- Cerclage, bands or isolated screws alone → high failure (Campbell)
- Gap between plate end and stem tip = new **stress riser** → **overlap** the stem
[[FIG: Fig 8.17 · 8.2

#### B2 — revise past the fracture
- Remove stem + cement, ETO if needed → long **cementless** porous-coated stem
[[FIG: Fig 8.18 · 8.2
- Bypass by **2 femoral diameters** or **4–6 cm** · 6 cm → more cortical contact (Prof Abdel Karim)
- Stem = **internal splint** → **cables first**, check stability, plate only if needed
- ETO indications → infection · **Vancouver B2** · femoral loosening · varus femur

#### B3 — loose stem, poor bone (Paprosky 3B/4)

- Options → impaction grafting, composite, proximal femoral replacement → 7 Loosening

#### Kit to have ready
- **Dual mobility cup** · cerclage cables, or **Biznoska bands** · **Wagner** stem · long cemented stem
[[FIG: Fig 8.19 · 8.2
- **NCB** periprosthetic plate · **flexible drill** · screws **3.5 and 4.5 mm**, every length

### Vancouver C & the locking plate
- Well-fixed stem → fixation, no revision → **B1 and C**
[[FIG: Fig 8.20 · 8.2
- Confirm the stem is stable → an unrecognised loose stem = **B2**
- Problems → stem and cement block screws · poor healing · bone defects

#### How the construct holds
- Principles → **relative stability** · long spanning plate · minimally invasive
- Distal → **bicortical** screws · beside the stem → **cables** or **unicortical** screws
[[FIG: Fig 8.21 · 8.2
- **Overlap the stem** → no unprotected bone between implant tips (Miller)
- Goals → stable fixation · keep fragments' soft tissue · restore length, offset, rotation

#### Devices
- Periprosthetic locking screws · variable-angle plates · trochanteric attachment devices
[[FIG: Fig 8.22 · 8.2
- **Proximal femoral hook plate** · distal femoral locking plate · retrograde locked nail
[[FIG: Fig 8.23 · 8.2

PITFALL — does a locking plate compress?
- Handbook → "hoop effect gives compression" · a locking plate = **internal fixator**, angular stability
- Say → "the locking plate splints with **relative stability**; the hoop effect belongs to the **cables**"

### Periprosthetic acetabular fractures
- **Uncommon but catastrophic** · more with **cementless** cups (Prof Kassem)
- Risks → **high impaction force** · revision · elliptical or threaded cup · osteoporosis · radiation · dysplasia
[[FIG: Fig 8.24 · 8.2

| Type | Circumstance |
|---|---|
| **1** | cup insertion |
| **2** | cup removal |
| **3** | traumatic |
| **4** | spontaneous |
| **5** | **pelvic discontinuity** |

#### Recognise it
- Intraoperative → **stress test** the cup, image · still in doubt → cup out, inspect
[[FIG: Fig 8.25 · 8.2
- Postoperative → **CT** · **CT angiography** before removing an intrapelvic cup
[[FIG: Fig 8.26 · 8.2
- Impaction fractures often show only after surgery → test the cup before closing

#### Treat by timing and cup stability

| When | Undisplaced + stable cup | Displaced + unstable cup |
|---|---|---|
| **Intraoperative** | extra **screws**, protected weight bearing | cup out → **plate** → cup back |
| **Postoperative** | conservative, protected weight bearing **6–8 weeks** | **ORIF** first → cup revision |

- Logic → as **pelvic discontinuity** → fix the columns, then judge the cup
[[FIG: Fig 8.27 · 8.2
- Displaced → plate alone · plate + cup · **multi-flanged** cage (ilium, ischium) or cup–cage
[[FIG: Fig 8.28 · 8.2
- Algorithm → wall vs column · stable vs unstable cup
[[FIG: Fig 8.29 · 8.2

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Loose = revise · B1 overlapping plate · B2 long stem · B3 rebuild · C plate · acetabulum: columns, then cup**

8.3.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "a stiff THA with bone in the soft tissues — what is it?"
- "**HO** (heterotopic ossification) → graded **Brooker I–IV** · grades III–IV → pain, stiffness."
- "High-risk patients only → **NSAID** or one **radiation** dose in the first days."
- "Formed bone → excise when **mature**, ≥6 months, with prophylaxis again."

### Heterotopic ossification
- High risk → men with **hypertrophic OA** · **ankylosing spondylitis** · **DISH** · previous HO
- DISH = diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis · approach changes where HO forms: abductors vs rotators
[[FIG: Fig 8.30 · 8.3

| Brooker grade (Campbell) | Picture |
|---|---|
| **I** | bone islands in soft tissue |
| **II** | spurs, gap **≥1 cm** |
| **III** | spurs, gap **<1 cm** |
| **IV** | **ankylosis** |

#### Prophylaxis early, excision late
- **Indomethacin** 25 mg ×3 daily, up to 6 weeks (Surgery of the Hip) · COX-2 equal
- **Radiation** → single **6–8 Gy** · ≤24 h before or ≤72 h after surgery (Miller)
- Both act on precursor cells only → formed bone can only be removed
- **Excision** → mature bone, ≥**6 months** · immature bone bleeds and recurs (Miller)

### Trochanteric osteotomy
- Indications → **extensile approach** · well-fixed cement or stem · ankylosis · HO · malposition
[[FIG: Fig 8.31 · 8.3
- **ETO** also → cement + **varus** femur → neutral reaming · hardware out · abductor tension
[[FIG: Fig 8.32 · 8.3
- Exposure → anterolateral (Watson-Jones), revision · **transfer** → more **abductor tension**
- Transfer → dysplasia · protrusio · recurrent dislocation · fusion converted to THA

#### Standard vs extended
- **Extended** → ≈10–12 cm, one-third of the circumference → long contact resists abductor pull
- Length → ≥**10 cm** from GT tip + **4–6 cm** diaphyseal fit · usually 12–16 cm (Prof Abdel Karim)
[[FIG: Fig 8.33 · 8.3
- Errors → too short, too long, no stem room · deformity → osteotomy **at the apex**
[[FIG: Fig 8.34 · 8.3
- **Trochanteric slide** → vastus lateralis stays on the fragment → counters abductor pull

### Trochanteric nonunion
- **3–8%** primaries · **9–13%** revisions · migration >**2 cm** → abductors fail even if united (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 8.35 · 8.3
- Abductors pull the fragment up with every step → it must heal under tension

#### Prevent it
- Good bone + a **large fragment** · refresh and pre-drill the bed
- **Rigid fixation** → ≥2–3 cables or wires · else double-wire cerclage · distal cable first
- Never **suture alone** → may not unite
[[FIG: Fig 8.36 · 8.3
- **Claw or cable-grip plate** + cables → hook over the tip + circumferential hold

PITFALL — wires or a plate?
- Prof Abdel Azeem → screws or plate, no wires · Prof Abdel Karim, Campbell → cables, wires standard
- Say → "**≥2–3 cables, or a claw plate + cables**; wire alone fails for a nonunion"

#### After surgery
- **Delayed weight bearing** · abduction brace · no active resisted abduction
- Proximal migration → slide keeps vastus lateralis: tethering · release a tight anterior pseudocapsule
- Broken wires or cables → fretting · fragments in the joint → **third-body wear**
[[FIG: Fig 8.37 · 8.3

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Brooker by the 1 cm gap · NSAID or 6–8 Gy early · excise at 6 months · ETO ≥10 cm · cables, brace**

| **IV** | **ankylosis** |

#### Prophylaxis early, excision late
- **Indomethacin** 25 mg ×3 daily, up to 6 weeks (Surgery of the Hip) · COX-2 equal
- **Radiation** → single **6–8 Gy** · ≤24 h before or ≤72 h after surgery (Miller)
- Both act on precursor cells only → formed bone can only be removed
- **Excision** → mature bone, ≥**6 months** · immature bone bleeds and recurs (Miller)

8.3.2.b:
- Indications → **extensile approach** · well-fixed cement or stem · ankylosis · HO · malposition
[[FIG: Fig 8.31 · 8.3
- **ETO** also → cement + **varus** femur → neutral reaming · hardware out · abductor tension
[[FIG: Fig 8.32 · 8.3
- Exposure → anterolateral (Watson-Jones), revision · **transfer** → more **abductor tension**
- Transfer → dysplasia · protrusio · recurrent dislocation · fusion converted to THA

#### Standard vs extended
- **Extended** → ≈10–12 cm, one-third of the circumference → long contact resists abductor pull
- Length → ≥**10 cm** from GT tip + **4–6 cm** diaphyseal fit · usually 12–16 cm (Prof Abdel Karim)
[[FIG: Fig 8.33 · 8.3
- Errors → too short, too long, no stem room · deformity → osteotomy **at the apex**
[[FIG: Fig 8.34 · 8.3
- **Trochanteric slide** → vastus lateralis stays on the fragment → counters abductor pull

8.3.3.b:
- **3–8%** primaries · **9–13%** revisions · migration >**2 cm** → abductors fail even if united (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 8.35 · 8.3
- Abductors pull the fragment up with every step → it must heal under tension

#### Prevent it
- Good bone + a **large fragment** · refresh and pre-drill the bed
- **Rigid fixation** → ≥2–3 cables or wires · else double-wire cerclage · distal cable first
- Never **suture alone** → may not unite
[[FIG: Fig 8.36 · 8.3
- **Claw or cable-grip plate** + cables → hook over the tip + circumferential hold

PITFALL — wires or a plate?
- Prof Abdel Azeem → screws or plate, no wires · Prof Abdel Karim, Campbell → cables, wires standard
- Say → "**≥2–3 cables, or a claw plate + cables**; wire alone fails for a nonunion"

#### After surgery
- **Delayed weight bearing** · abduction brace · no active resisted abduction
- Proximal migration → slide keeps vastus lateralis: tethering · release a tight anterior pseudocapsule
- Broken wires or cables → fretting · fragments in the joint → **third-body wear**
[[FIG: Fig 8.37 · 8.3

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Brooker by the 1 cm gap · NSAID or 6–8 Gy early · excise at 6 months · ETO ≥10 cm · cables, brace**
